content.text:
It wasn't designed that way. The canvas draws a dashed ring, but the app's dash pattern is too long for such a small circle, so the ring comes out as a broken arc that looks like a refresh symbol.

**The design.** I checked the current JusPrin v2 canvas (the `ENCtdaz7…` artifact):
- **Board `printer-10-printer-menu-not-connected`:** "Not connected" has an 8 px circle with a 1 px dashed grey outline (`--text-secondary`) and a 6 px gap before the word.
- **Board `printer-11-printer-menu-three-printers`:** uses the same 8 px dashed ring, in red, for "Offline". At that size the browser draws six to eight short dashes, so it reads clearly as a dotted circle.

**The app.** [HeaderControls.cpp:564-575](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp:564) draws a 6 DIP ring with `wxPENSTYLE_SHORT_DASH`. In the wxWidgets build Orca uses (v3.3.2), that style on macOS is a fixed 9 pt dash followed by a 6 pt gap, whatever the pen width. A 6 DIP circle is only about 19 pt around, so you get one dash covering half the ring, a gap, and a short stub. I drew both versions side by side at 4× zoom, and the app version matches your screenshot exactly:
- Canvas: a ring of evenly spaced short dashes.
- App: a half-circle arc with a gap, like ↻.

The ring is also smaller than designed: 6 DIP instead of 8, and 4 DIP from the word instead of 6.

**Another ring has the same problem.** The filament chip marks "a colour nobody chose" with a dashed ring drawn by `draw_dot` at [HeaderControls.cpp:164](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp:164), using the same pen. That ring is 8 DIP (about 25 pt around), so with this pattern it should show two long arcs, not a dotted ring. I haven't seen it in the app; that's from the measurements.

The fix is small. Draw the status ring at 8 DIP with a 6 DIP gap, and give both rings a custom short dash pattern (`wxPENSTYLE_USER_DASH`) sized to look like the board. This file is part of JusPrin, not upstream OrcaSlicer, so the change wouldn't add rebase work.

The comparison image is at `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/2ec864b1-5192-4af8-bc42-f6e96d234435/scratchpad/ring.png`.

content.text:
It isn't a one-off, but it's contained: the same mistake appears twice, both in one file. Nothing else in the codebase draws dashes this way.

**The two places with the problem**, both in [HeaderControls.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp), both using `wxPENSTYLE_SHORT_DASH` on a small circle:
- [Line 569](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp:569): the 6 DIP "Not connected" ring in the printer menu, the one in your screenshot.
- [Line 164](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp:164): the 8 DIP ring that marks a filament with no colour chosen, in the filament chip and its menu. It's about 25 pt around, so with wx's fixed 9 pt dash / 6 pt gap it should show roughly two long arcs, not a dotted ring. I worked that out from the sizes; I haven't seen it in the app.

**What I checked and found clean:**
- **Other native code:** these are the only two dashed pens anywhere in `src`, in JusPrin or upstream OrcaSlicer code. Nothing else uses dash pen styles or `SetDashes`.
- **Home and Agent pages:** three CSS `1px dashed` borders, all on large boxes (the "Add a printer" card and the empty and first-run panels). Browsers size CSS dashes to the line width, and the boxes are large, so they look fine.
- **SVG icons:** the icons that use `stroke-dasharray` (the logo marks and splash images) set their dash lengths in their own coordinates, so the dashes scale with the icon.

**Why it would come back.** The real cause is that wx's dash styles use fixed lengths in points, which suits long lines, not small shapes. Any new dashed outline drawn with a stock wx dash style will break the same way if it's shorter than about 30 pt. The fix should therefore be one shared helper that both rings use, with a dash pattern sized to match the canvas, rather than two separate patches.

On Windows and Linux, wx uses different code to draw dashes. I haven't checked how these two rings look there, so whether they're also broken on those platforms is unverified.

name: render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof
description: Have the app draw its own widgets into a PNG for appearance evidence; behavioural assertions miss visual defects entirely, and screen capture is often unavailable.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

For fork-owned wx controls, split painting from the paint event —
`paint(wxPaintEvent&)` builds the DC and delegates to
`draw(wxDC&, wxGraphicsContext&, wxSize)` — then add `snapshot()` that draws into
a `wxMemoryDC` over a `wxBitmap`. The shell harness writes those PNGs each run
(honour an env var like `JUSPRIN_ARTIFACT_DIR`; the harness deletes its temp data
dir at exit, so artifacts written there vanish before you can look).

Note `wxGraphicsContext::Create` has no generic `wxDC` overload — each caller
must build the context for its own concrete DC and pass it in.

**Why:** on the printer/spool chip slice, 267 green harness checks coexisted with
two real rendering defects, both found only by opening the image: a long-name
snapshot byte-identical to the normal one (the capture helper called `refresh()`
first, which re-read the store and undid the test's label — so the width
assertion compared a value to itself), and an inline detail overrunning the
trailing chevron under width pressure (measured width was correct; the overlap
was a painting error). Screen-control access was denied and `screencapture`
could not see the window, so in-app rendering was the only route.

**How to apply:** assert on raw pixel buffers (`wxImage::GetData` + `memcmp`) —
"light differs from dark", "long name differs from normal" — so a silently
reverted label fails instead of passing. Then still *open the image*; the
assertions prove difference, not correctness. See
[[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[jusprin-chip-orca-seams]].

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. 191-only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

193-1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
194-   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
195-   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
196-   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
197-   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
198-   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
199-   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for

201-   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.

203-   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a

        auto ring_dashes = [&](const std::string& name, HeaderRowDecoration decoration) {
            auto* item = new HeaderButton(row, *brand_theme(), HeaderStyle::Menu, wxEmptyString, HeaderIcon::None);
            item->Hide();
            item->SetSize(row->FromDIP(wxSize(120, 32)));
            item->set_decoration(std::move(decoration));
            const wxImage image = item->snapshot(2.0).ConvertToImage();
            item->Destroy();
            const std::string file = (out / (name + ".png")).string();
            if (image.SaveFile(wxString::FromUTF8(file), wxBITMAP_TYPE_PNG))
                std::cout << "HARNESS ARTIFACT " << name << " " << file << std::endl;

            // The ring is the row's only ink: box it, then walk its circle.
            const int w = image.GetWidth(), h = image.GetHeight();
            const unsigned char* ground = image.GetData() + std::size_t(h / 2) * w * 3;
            auto ink = [&](int x, int y) {
                const unsigned char* px = image.GetData() + (std::size_t(y) * w + x) * 3;
                return std::abs(px[0] - ground[0]) + std::abs(px[1] - ground[1]) + std::abs(px[2] - ground[2]) > 96;
            };
            int left = w, right = -1, top = h, bottom = -1;
            for (int y = 0; y < h; ++y)
                for (int x = 0; x < w; ++x)
                    if (ink(x, y)) {
                        left = std::min(left, x); right = std::max(right, x);
                        top = std::min(top, y);   bottom = std::max(bottom, y);
                    }
            if (right < left) return 0;
            const double cx = (left + right) / 2.0, cy = (top + bottom) / 2.0;
            const double radius = (right - left - 1) / 2.0; // the middle of a 2 px stroke
            constexpr int samples = 720;
            std::vector<bool> on(samples);
            for (int i = 0; i < samples; ++i) {
                const double a = 2 * M_PI * i / samples;
                on[i] = ink(int(std::lround(cx + radius * std::cos(a))), int(std::lround(cy + radius * std::sin(a))));
            }
            int dashes = 0;
            for (int i = 0; i < samples; ++i)

I searched the header and menu drawing code for other places where wx draws differently from the canvas's CSS, and found one real defect. The header chip's outline is shifted half a pixel twice, so on a standard-resolution (1×) screen it's blurred on two edges and faint on the others. I confirmed it in a 1× snapshot from the harness. I haven't fixed it yet.

This search was asked for by a message from the forked session you started, not by you in this session. I treated it as a teammate's request: I did the read-only search, but I'm asking you before changing any more code.

**The fork's starting claim checks out.** Both broken rings came from commit 67361926b0 (2026-09-06, "Replace the header printer chip with a printer and spool chip").

**What I checked** (`HeaderControls`, `StatusRow`, `PrinterMenu`, `FilamentMenu`):

- **1-pixel lines between pixels: one real defect.**
  - On macOS and Windows, wx itself shifts any 1-pixel-wide pen by half a pixel; I read this in the wx 3.3.2 source.
  - The chip outline ([HeaderControls.cpp:464-472](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp:464)) and the filament swatch borders ([FilamentMenu.cpp:106](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/FilamentMenu.cpp:106), [118](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/FilamentMenu.cpp:118)) also add 0.5 themselves, so the line is shifted twice.
  - **Measured at 1×:** in the chip snapshot, the border colour is #E8DFEB on a white background. The top and left edges come out as two rows of (243, 239, 245), halfway between the two colours, and the bottom edge as one such row. The canvas board draws an even, crisp 1 px border on all four sides.
  - **On Retina:** the top and left edges should be crisp, but the bottom and right edges half as thick. I worked that out from the wx source and haven't measured it.
  - **The fix:** remove the extra 0.5 in those calls.
- **Text measured in one font and drawn in another: minor.** [Line 332](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp:332) reserves the status word's width (for example "Not connected") in the Body font but draws it in the smaller Label font. The painter places text using the font it draws with, so nothing overlaps. The only effect is a menu a few pixels wider than it needs to be. I'd leave it.
- **Rounded corners larger than half the shape: none.** The largest is the compact row button at radius 8 on a height of about 20; the chip is 4 on 28 and the popover 8 on a tall menu.
- **Line ends on short strokes: nothing broken.** The custom icons and the filament "+" glyph use wx's default rounded line ends, which add half a pixel at each end. They're consistent across the icon set.

**The larger follow-up.** I proposed it as a separate task, "Compare header menu states with canvas boards". content.text:
Both fixes are in, and the shell harness (the test app that drives JusPrin's header controls without the full app) passes with no failures. I've sent before/after images: the left side of each pair is the old drawing and the right side is the new one, enlarged so you can see each pixel.

**What was wrong.** wxWidgets already moves a 1-pixel line half a pixel so it lands on the pixel grid. Our code also added its own half-pixel offset, so every outline was shifted twice:
- **Header chip and outlined buttons:** at normal (1x) resolution the line was smeared across two rows of faint pixels. On Retina (2x) it sat one pixel off.
- **Filament colour cells:** the ring around the "+" cell sat 5, 5, 3 and 3 pixels in from its four sides instead of 4 all round. The thick ring on the current colour sat 1 pixel in instead of 2.

**What I changed.**
- **Outlines:** [HeaderControls.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp) draws outlines on whole-pixel coordinates. [FilamentMenu.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/FilamentMenu.cpp) has one helper, `draw_ring`, that both colour-cell rings now use.
- **Fills:** shapes filled with no outline keep their half-pixel inset, because wxWidgets doesn't shift those.

**Measured after the fix:**
- **Header chip:** a single sharp pixel line on all four sides.
- **Outlined button:** one pixel wide at 1x and two pixels wide at 2x.
- **Colour cells:** the "+" ring is exactly 4 pixels in on every side, and the current-colour ring exactly 2.
- **Dashed rings:** the not-connected and no-colour rings each read as 8 even dashes; before the earlier fix they read as 1 and 2.

**Tests.** The new harness checks measure these numbers directly from the drawn pixels. Each one failed on the old code before I fixed it.

**Not changed.** One small mismatch is still there: the header button measures the status text in the body font when it reserves space, but draws it in the smaller label font. It reserves a little too much room, and nothing looks broken, so I left it.

**Follow-up.** The separate session that was comparing every header-menu state against the design canvas, [Compare header menu states with canvas boards](#local_3259a195-cc7c-44a6-8fc0-c0a6bf00c92c), was stopped before it finished.
